open_questions: TIC radius 0.402 Rsun is small; stellar_radius could not provide Gaia FLAME radius to refine planet parameters and stellar density penalty 467.2 remains due to the long ratio 1.622 duration vs 1.227 h central.

The 1.87-d signal is ~1.33 x the detected 1.4025-d rotation and shows a strong spot-like phase curve (amplitude ~depth); simultaneous spot modeling is needed to confirm the transit shape is not spot-distorted.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 2.76 Earth-radius dip every 1.87 days on a nearby M dwarf that looks flat-bottomed, with no odd/even change and no reliable second eclipse. Images put the dip on the target and rule out nearby eclipsing stars, while the large brightness swings outside eclipse match the star's own spot period of 1.40 days. With Gaia radius checks pending, a small planet remains the best explanation.

reasons.why: difference imaging puts the dip on the target and all neighbours that could cause it are >31 sigma from the centroid; plausible_within_1px 0 and could_cause_within_1px 0 supports a planet on the target over a neighbour blend.
boxy/ flat-bottom profile (v_sigma negative) favours a transiting body over a grazing stellar eclipse, despite duration ratio 1.622.

radius is planet-sized, much too small to be a stellar eclipse; secondary is below 5 sigma and well below the dominant brightening (large phase_curve chi2 194.7 dof 9, amplitude 3917 ppm ratio 0.9898 off-target), consistent with spot-driven variability rather than a stable secondary eclipse; odd_even.diff_sigma 0.5768 shows no odd/even difference.
reasons.value: rp_rearth 2.76 (R*, 0.4021 Rsun), secondary snr 4.712 depth_over_dip 0.2462, best_brightening_snr 10.61

reasons.why: period is not an exact multiple of the spot period and the large variability amplitude in sector 68 (45489 ppm) drives the phase_curve signal and is atypical for a close binary, leaving a planet as the best explanation despite the short 1.991 h duration.
